purpose: Questions authored independently of the implementation. The review and validation groups record separate evaluations; both have now been inspected and must not be described as untouched in future tuning. Required source text measures retrieval, not generated-answer accuracy. Use scripts/score_search.py --group review or --group validation to score a group separately.

cases.query: How do I stop gradients from flowing back through part of my computation?
support: The operation is the identity but it prevents gradients from flowing through the array.

cases.query: Can I set an upper bound on how much memory MLX uses while my training runs?
support: The memory limit is a guideline for the maximum amount of memory to use during graph evaluation.

cases.query: My backward pass runs out of memory on a deep model. Can I recompute intermediate values instead of keeping them all?
support: Use this to reduce memory use for gradient computations at the expense of increased computation.

cases.query: I appended results to an outer Python list inside a compiled function and now printing that list crashes. What is going on?
support: The placeholder does not have any data; it is only used to build the computation graph.

cases.query: In a training loop, how often should I force MLX to actually run the computation, and is a very large graph a problem?
support: Luckily, a wide range of compute graph sizes work pretty well with MLX

cases.query: I indexed past the end of an array on the GPU and got garbage instead of an exception. Why is there no error?
support: The reason for the lack of bounds checking is that exceptions cannot propagate from the GPU.

cases.query: When several updates hit the same index in an indexed add, only one of them seems to apply. How do I accumulate all of them?
support: As a result, assigning to the same index ignores all but one update.

cases.query: Do I have to copy my arrays from CPU memory to GPU memory before running an operation on the GPU?
support: In MLX, rather than moving arrays to devices, you specify the device when you run the operation.

cases.query: How do I checkpoint my optimizer so I can resume training with the same Adam moments?
support: To serialize an optimizer, save its state. To load an optimizer, load and set the saved state.

cases.query: Can I save a traced MLX function to disk and run it later from a different front-end?
support: MLX has an API to export and import functions to and from a file.

cases.query: I only want to train the attention weights of my transformer and leave everything else fixed.
support: Freezing a parameter means not computing gradients for it.

cases.query: I want attention scores biased by how far apart two tokens are so the model extrapolates to longer sequences. Is there a built-in layer?
support: ALiBi adds a static, non-learnable bias matrix to attention scores proportional to the distance between query and key tokens.

cases.query: Can I use one optimizer for my embedding weights and a different one for the rest of the model?
support: to make it easy to use different optimizers for different weights

cases.query: How do I build a learning rate that warms up linearly and then switches over to a cosine decay?
support: Join multiple schedules to create a new schedule.

cases.query: Is there a fused cross entropy loss for token logits in MLX, and does it also work on the CPU?
support: The CPU falls back to the unfused version, which reduces in the dtype of the logits.

cases.query: In data-parallel training across Macs, how do I average gradients without sending lots of tiny messages?
support: This helper enables concatenating several gradients of small arrays to one big all reduce call for better networking performance.

cases.query: I create a custom Metal kernel inside my model's forward pass and every call is slow. What is the right pattern?
support: Every time you make a kernel, a new Metal library is created and possibly JIT compiled.

cases.query: When adding a custom op in C++, where does the actual CPU or GPU compute code go versus the user-facing function?
support: Operations in MLX build the computation graph. Primitives provide the rules for evaluating and transforming the graph.

cases.query: My LoRA fine-tune keeps running out of memory on a 32 GB Mac. What can I change to make it fit?
support: Here are some tips to reduce memory use should you need to do so

cases.query: During fine-tuning I only care about the model's answer, not the prompt. Can I leave the prompt out of the loss?
support: The default training computes a loss for every token in the sample.

cases.query: I finished LoRA training. How do I merge the adapter weights into the base model and publish the result?
support: You can generate a model fused with the low-rank adapters

cases.query: Plain 4-bit conversion hurts my model's accuracy. Are there smarter ways to quantize with less quality loss?
support: To reduce the quality loss from quantization MLX LM has several options

cases.query: If I start the local server with a Hugging Face repo id that I have not downloaded yet, will it fetch it?
support: The model will be downloaded from the provided Hugging Face repo if it is not already in the local cache.

cases.query: Reading a very long prompt makes my memory spike. How can I lower the peak memory during prompt processing?
support: Smaller steps use less peak memory while the prompt is read, at some cost to prompt processing speed.

cases.query: The tool warns that generating with my model will be slow even though the model fits in RAM. Is there a system setting that speeds it up?
support: If the model fits in RAM then it can often be sped up by increasing the system wired memory limit.

cases.query: In the Python API, how do I supply my own function for picking the next token?
support: A sampler is any callable which accepts a possibly batched logits array and returns an array of sampled tokens.

cases.query: After pip install, can MLX Data load video files and pull data from S3 without extra setup?
support: should install the package together with the necessary dependencies to read audio, images, video and remote content from S3

cases.query: My dataset is huge, lives on remote storage and is nested, so I cannot index into it randomly. What should I build the pipeline on?
support: Often datasets are too big, stored remotely or are nested in ways that prevent random access.

cases.query: How can I switch dataset transforms on or off from command-line flags without a mess of if statements?
support: A common issue when writing pipelines is configuring them according to the command line or configuration arguments.

cases.query: Tokenizing text in my data pipeline with a Python tokenizer only uses one core. How do I speed it up?
support: subject to the GIL which means that effectively only one sample can be tokenized at a time

cases.query: In my MLX training loop I append loss.item() to a Python list before evaluating the updated parameters. Does collecting that scalar run any computation at that point?
cases.expected_answer: Yes. Calling item() evaluates the scalar loss. At that point it can be a partial evaluation that computes only the forward pass.
support: Calling array.item() on a scalar array will also evaluate it.

cases.query: On Apple silicon, a GPU operation in my MLX program consumes the result of an earlier CPU operation. Do I need to copy the array between devices or add the dependency myself?
cases.expected_answer: No explicit array transfer is needed between those devices. MLX inserts the dependency between their streams so the consumer waits for its input.
support: without needing to move them from one memory location to another
MLX will automatically insert a dependency between the two streams

cases.query: I ported NumPy code that takes b = a[:] and modifies b. Should the original MLX array a change too?
cases.expected_answer: No. An MLX slice creates a copy rather than a view, so modifying that slice does not modify the original array.
support: slicing an array creates a copy, not a view.

cases.query: Assigning x[mask] = 0 works in MLX. Can I also use x[mask] to return just the elements selected by the boolean mask?
cases.expected_answer: Boolean mask indexing is supported for assignment only, so the corresponding selection expression is not supported.
support: Boolean mask based indexing is supported for assignment only

cases.query: I'm compiling an MLX training step that includes Dropout. Besides the model and optimizer, what state needs to be captured for the random sampling?
cases.expected_answer: Include mx.random.state in the state captured by compile().
support: include mx.random.state in the state captured by compile()

cases.query: I want to vectorize f(example, weights) over a batch of examples while using the same weights for every example. How do I tell MLX not to add a mapped dimension to the weights argument?
cases.expected_answer: Use vmap with in_axes=(0, None). None marks the weights input as not vectorized.
support: If the value is None then the corresponding input(s) are not vmapped.

cases.query: My MLX loss has two positional parameter arrays and a trainable keyword argument. How do I request derivatives for selected positional arguments and for that keyword argument?
cases.expected_answer: Use grad's argnums to select positional argument indices and argnames to select keyword arguments.
support: Specify the index (or indices) of the positional arguments
Specify keyword arguments of fun to compute gradients with respect to.

cases.query: I'm calling layer.freeze(keys="bias"). How can I keep its submodules trainable and make a missing bias key raise a validation error?
cases.expected_answer: Set recurse=False to avoid freezing submodules and strict=True to validate that the requested key exists.
support: If True then freeze the parameters of the submodules as well.
If set to True validate that the passed keys exist.

cases.query: I'm using Module.load_weights(strict=False) for a partial checkpoint. Does that mode still protect me from loading a tensor with the wrong shape?
cases.expected_answer: No. In non-strict mode only weights contained in the model are loaded, and their shapes are not checked.
support: only the weights actually contained in the model are loaded and shapes are not checked.

cases.query: I already have the gradient tree from nn.value_and_grad and an MLX optimizer object. What call applies those gradients to the network itself?
cases.expected_answer: Call optimizer.update(model, gradients). It updates the model with the new parameters.
support: update the model with the new parameters.

cases.query: My image batches currently have PyTorch's NCHW layout. What axis order should I provide to an MLX Conv2d layer?
cases.expected_answer: Provide NHWC, with channels last.
support: The channels are expected to be last i.e. the input shape should be NHWC

cases.query: For cross_entropy in MLX, my logits are shaped (batch, classes) and the targets are integer class labels. Should the target array be (batch,) or (batch, 1) with the default class axis?
cases.expected_answer: Use (batch,). The default class axis is -1, and class-index targets omit that dimension from the logits shape.
support: targets shape should match the logits shape with the axis dimension removed.

cases.query: I have one explicit MLX random key and need four subkeys for separate random operations. Which function makes them, and where does the number of subkeys appear in its result?
cases.expected_answer: Call mx.random.split(key, num=4). It returns an array whose first dimension is num.
support: The array of sub keys with num as its first dimension.

cases.query: I'm implementing grouped-query attention with MLX's fast attention primitive. Do I need to repeat the key and value heads until they have as many heads as the queries?
cases.expected_answer: No. For grouped-query or multi-query attention, pass the key and value inputs without pre-tiling them to match q.
support: For Grouped Query Attention and Multi-Query Attention, the k and v inputs should not be pre-tiled to match q .

cases.query: Can mlx.core.quantize handle a flat vector directly? What shape restrictions should I check before passing a weight array and a group size?
cases.expected_answer: The input must have at least two dimensions, and its last dimension must be divisible by group_size. A flat vector does not meet that contract.
support: quantize only supports inputs with two or more dimensions with the last dimension divisible by group_size

cases.query: My MLX matrix multiplication inputs and outputs say float32, but I need to rule out reduced-precision matrix arithmetic. What setting requests full float32 when I launch the program?
cases.expected_answer: Launch the process with MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 to keep those operations in full float32.
support: To keep these operations in full float32 , set MLX_ENABLE_TF32 to 0 when launching the process:

cases.query: I'm saving several named MLX arrays as safetensors. Do I pass them as separate positional arrays like savez, or does the writer expect a different input structure?
cases.expected_answer: save_safetensors takes a dictionary mapping string names to arrays.
support: The functions save_safetensors() and save_gguf() are similar to savez()
they take as input a dict of string names to arrays

cases.query: Converting an MLX bfloat16 array with np.array raises a buffer-format error. What conversion should I do before handing the values to NumPy?
cases.expected_answer: Convert the MLX array to float16 or float32 first because NumPy does not support bfloat16 arrays.
support: Since NumPy does not support bfloat16 arrays, you will need to convert to float16 or float32 first:

cases.query: I have a linear system A X = B and want MLX to compute X directly instead of explicitly forming an inverse. Which linear algebra function should I use?
cases.expected_answer: Use mlx.core.linalg.solve(a, b), which returns the unique solution of AX = B.
support: The unique solution to the system AX = B .

cases.query: I want the memory high-water mark for one section of an MLX program instead of the whole process lifetime. How do I start a new measurement window and read its peak in bytes?
cases.expected_answer: Call reset_peak_memory() before the section, then get_peak_memory(). The getter reports bytes and records its maximum since the last reset.
support: Reset the peak memory to zero.
Get the peak amount of used memory in bytes.
since the last call to reset_peak_memory()

cases.query: In a Python application using MLX LM, how can I print the generated text as it arrives instead of waiting for the complete answer string?
cases.expected_answer: Iterate over stream_generate(model, tokenizer, prompt, ...) and print each response.text as it arrives.

cases.query: I cached a long document with MLX LM and now supply a new question when generating. Does the new prompt replace the cached document, or is it added after it?
cases.expected_answer: The cached prompt is a prefix to the supplied prompt, so the new question follows the cached context.
support: The cached prompt is treated as a prefix to the supplied prompt.

cases.query: When fine-tuning with mlx_lm.lora, how do I train only on the assistant completion rather than the prompt? Is that option available for a plain text dataset too?
cases.expected_answer: Pass --mask-prompt. It is supported only for chat and completion datasets, not plain text datasets.
support:
compute loss for just the completion by passing
`--mask-prompt`

cases.query: If I enable KV-cache quantization on the MLX LM HTTP server, can it still batch several clients' generation requests together?
cases.expected_answer: No. With --kv-bits enabled, the server processes requests one at a time because the quantized KV cache does not support batching.
support: A quantized KV cache does not support batching.
one at a time when you set `--kv-bits`.

cases.query: How can I inspect just a selected family of downloaded MLX LM models from the command line, and where are those local downloads stored?
cases.expected_answer: Use mlx_lm.manage --scan --pattern with the desired model pattern. The models are stored in the Hugging Face cache.
support:
They
are stored in the Hugging Face cache.

cases.query: I want to try different high-bit and low-bit choices with MLX LM dynamic quantization on the same model. What can I reuse so I don't have to estimate which layers are sensitive again?
cases.expected_answer: Reuse the JSON file of per-layer sensitivities produced by dynamic quantization, passing its path with --sensitivities.
support: The script also saves a JSON file with each layer's sensitivities
`--sensitivities`: A path to a precomputed sensitivities file.

cases.query: In MLX Data, one input needs a known length and random access, while another is consumed continuously and may never end. Should I use the same container type for both?
cases.expected_answer: Use a Buffer for the input requiring a known length and random access. A Stream is a potentially infinite iterable suitable for the continuous input.
support: They have a known length and they can be shuffled or accessed in random order.
A Stream is a potentially infinite iterable of samples.

cases.query: My token sequences vary greatly in length, so fixed-size batches in MLX Data waste a lot of padding. What stream operation can keep roughly the same amount of token work in each batch?
cases.expected_answer: Use Stream.dynamic_batch. It targets approximately the same number of total elements per batch and reduces padding waste for variable-size samples.
support: Dynamic batching returns batches with approximately the same number of total elements.
minimize padding and waste of computation

cases.query: I want MLX Data to load samples in background threads, but evaluation must see them in the original buffer order. Which prefetch operation provides that ordering guarantee?
cases.expected_answer: Use Buffer.ordered_prefetch, which fetches in background threads while preserving the original order.
support: Fetch samples in background threads, while preserving original ordering.

cases.query: For each sample in an MLX Data buffer I want to split an array's first dimension into several shards, but keep the original array under its current key. How can I store the reshaped result separately?
cases.expected_answer: Use Buffer.shard on the input key with num_shards, and set a nonempty output_key so the result goes to a different key instead of overwriting the input.
support: Split the first dimension in num_shards .
If it is not empty then write the result to this key instead of overwriting key .
